baselineFindings.finding: Resolver checks revoked/expiry but not current issuer access or original report student/owner/intake. Credential-free reproduction resolves after creator removal and follows reassigned context.
Omitted expires_in_days inserts null, although the saved-report UI supplies 30 days.
Current tracking checks only revoked, not expiry or current issuer access.

Update is scoped by report ID but has no affected-row assertion or observed-context compare. RLS/identity trigger restrict unauthorized writes; success feedback for zero rows and stale owner relinks require separate review.

Content revision binds id/student/content, not intake association or other mutable generation inputs. New student-aware save closes its named student/content race, not all provider-input provenance races.

proposedBehavior: Before insertion lock referenced report FOR SHARE; require current explicit student access for linked report or ownership for unlinked report; overwrite supplied bindings with actual student/owner/intake.
Use reviewed can_access_student actor helper, with no management shortcut; apply the same predicate to resolver and tracking, retaining service-role-only RPC execution and audience projection.
Default newly inserted links to 30 days when omitted; retain current API upper bound of 365 days at database boundary.
Revoke links on report student/owner/intake change, including unlink/relink and change-away/change-back; ordinary content changes remain live.

Retire all existing unbound legacy links as revoked in the same transaction, so existing screens do not label unusable links as active. Creators must issue replacements; no historical context is guessed. This is a proposed existing-data change requiring explicit future rollout authorization.

User-selected permanent closure: source-table hooks cover collaboration/consent deletion, reassignment and status changes plus loss of student ownership/self identity. Serialize access-loss checks per student with transaction advisory locks, then lock reports to catch in-flight mints. Retain links when another genuine access path remains. Revocation participates in the original removal transaction and rolls back with it.

validation.engine: Disposable native PostgreSQL and credential-free local PGlite
validation.ci: Existing automatic migration replay now includes local and native proposal cases plus rollback-only integration after all canonical checks. No canonical migration added.
validation.preliminaryHarnessCorrections: Two initial fixture errors (duplicate insert column and untyped unused parameter) corrected without changing expected denials. Single-case check initially omitted local module path; corrected invocation passed.

localPGlite.reason: Nine real multi-session cases require native PostgreSQL

initialNativeFailure.finding: Tracking waiting behind a committed revocation incremented view_count because the STABLE eligibility helper saw an older statement snapshot. This was a real proposal defect, not a harness failure.
initialNativeFailure.correction: Recheck mutable revoked/context_bound/expiry directly on the UPDATE target so row-lock rechecks reject a concurrently invalidated token. Strict regression retained; concurrent expiry case added.

compatibilityAndOpenWork: Legacy-link proposal is now concrete: revoke preexisting unbound links in the migration transaction and require recreation. Existing UI filters revoked links, avoiding an active-but-unresolvable listing. User must review this data change in any future rollout authorization; no legacy rows have been changed outside disposable CI.

User chose permanent closure. The local proposal now latches revocation when the last explicit access path is lost; re-addition requires fresh links. This behavior passed native multi-session validation and is not yet deployed.

Before rollout: prepare canonical migration/exact ledger and verified prerequisite/body/grant preflight, update the exact private-routine inventory, and rerun the full canonical migration chain. Existing canonical verifier assumes service-forbidden functions are triggers; new private boolean/void helpers require explicit narrow inventory assertions, not blanket grant relaxation. No release-ready migration/rollout packet exists yet.

Remaining direct-client report writers/intake association/provenance races need separate scoped review, not permission expansion.
Channel member removal and optional chat-history retention remain distinct from bearer report links.

pendingUserPreference.question: When someone loses student access, should their report links remain permanently closed if they are later re-added?
pendingUserPreference.recommended: Permanent closure; create fresh links after re-addition
pendingUserPreference.currentDraft: Permanent revocation after losing the final explicit student-access path; restored access permits fresh links but never reactivates old ones
pendingUserPreference.scope: Report bearer links only, separate from retained chat history
pendingUserPreference.selected: Permanently close their links; create new ones if re-added
